system: rask HTR Model · Forward Pass + Training Step
audience: ML engineers working on the HTR model (TrOCR-style image-encoder → text-decoder)

mode_descriptions.train: Training loop on Ray Train (TorchTrainer · DDP · GPU). Dropout on, autograd on; DataLoader/Ray Data streams batches, loss is computed, backward + optimizer.step() update weights, checkpoints are written and promoted to HF Hub.
mode_descriptions.eval: Inference / validation. model.eval() disables dropout, everything runs under torch.no_grad(); loss and optimizer are skipped (eval reports CER/WER as a metric, not a training signal); batch size drops to 1 for per-page transcription.

flows.name: Forward Pass (page image → text)
flows.purpose: Altitude 1: the model as a flow. A scanned page tensor runs through the image encoder, transformer decoder, and output head, then is decoded to text. Tensor shapes ride along as payloads. Same path in train and eval — eval just runs it under no_grad with batch size 1.
step_outline: text → text       : argmax / beam decode → "transcribed text"

flows.name: Training Step (one optimizer.step())
flows.purpose: Altitude 2: the training loop for a single step. DataLoader / Ray Data yields a batch, the model runs the forward pass, CTC/CE loss is computed against targets, loss.backward() fills grads (all-reduced across Ray Train workers), optimizer.step() updates weights, then the checkpoint is written and promoted to HF Hub. Train-only — eval skips loss/backward/optimizer.
step_outline: raytrain → data    : worker pulls batch [B,3,H,W] + targets
data → backbone    : forward pass through encoder/decoder/head → logits [B,T,vocab]
head → loss        : CTC / CrossEntropy(logits, targets) → scalar
optim → raytrain   : DDP all-reduce grads across workers
optim → backbone   : AdamW optimizer.step() · lr sched → updated weights
raytrain → ckpt    : write state_dict + optimizer + step
ckpt → hfhub       : promote checkpoint → push to model registry

flows.name: Eval Step (validation / inference)
flows.purpose: Inference path: model.eval() (dropout off) under torch.no_grad(), batch size 1. Runs the same forward pass but reports CER/WER as a metric instead of a training loss — no backward, no optimizer, no checkpoint.
step_outline: backbone → text : forward pass → logits [1,T,vocab] → decoded text
head → loss     : compare to reference → CER / WER metric (no grad)

lessons: Two altitudes, one model: forward_pass draws the model as a flow (encoder → decoder → head → decode); train_step wraps that same path in a loss + backward + optimizer.step() + checkpoint loop. Don't try to show both at full detail in one flow — toggle between them.

Tensor shapes are payloads, not nodes: [B,3,H,W] → [B,768,h,w] → [B,T,768] → [B,T,vocab] → string ride on the port/payload, keeping the node count low. This is a high-level model lens — for a per-layer graph reach for torchview / Netron / torchinfo / PlotNeuralNet instead.

train vs eval is a real mode toggle: eval disables loss, optimizer, and dropout, runs under no_grad, and swaps batch size to 1. node.modes / only_mode keep the loss, optimizer, Ray Train, checkpoint, and HF Hub nodes from showing in eval where they don't apply.

Six roles, no more: the three model blocks (backbone / decoder / head) all share the embed role (amber); loss and Ray Train are compute; DataLoader and optimizer are seed (one-shot per step); checkpoint store, decoded text, and HF Hub share vector. Distinct blocks, not distinct colors.
The HF Hub node is the model registry — checkpoints are promoted to it rather than drawing a separate registry node, mirroring how the ingest pipeline reuses the same HF Hub for pulling weights.
